headline: High-risk filesystem and Git overlap from ECC; prompt-injection and cascading-error risks are limited by godot_rl_agents' no-network, no-IO profile.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ECC can read/write files, use MCP, and process session/skill files, so a manual or file-based bridge could carry malicious instructions into its workflow. godot_rl_agents exposes no IO surfaces or shared channel, so the pair lacks a documented direct injection path; the risk is limited to unusual bridging by the operator.
conditions: IF the operator copies agent_a output into a file or prompt consumed by agent_b
IF a shared filesystem or clipboard is introduced between the agents
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Disable copy-paste of untrusted agent output into ECC skills or MCP inputs
Review any imported text for instruction-like content before reuse
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging to shared artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: ECC touches session summaries, git history, code, and security findings, but godot_rl_agents has no documented data classes or network egress. With no shared workspace or outbound path on agent_b, leakage is not evidenced as a default pairwise channel; any exposure would require an external bridge not shown here.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or repository
IF sensitive files are manually transferred from ECC into another system
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent
Avoid placing secrets in ECC-managed files
Audit any exported logs before sharing
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the orchestrator

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ECC has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and allowlisted network egress, while godot_rl_agents is documented with no IO surfaces and no write capabilities. The pair does not show a direct write-write collision, but ECC's mutable Git/filesystem actions can still conflict with any external process touching the same repo or files; uncertainty keeps this above low.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to modify the same git checkout
IF an external process writes to files ECC is editing
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate repository clone
Pause one agent before the other edits shared files
Use git locks or a single-writer policy

D_cascading_error.rationale: ECC can generate and modify code, docs, and security findings, but godot_rl_agents has no documented action-taking or output-consuming surface. Without a verified pipeline where B treats A's output as authoritative, cascading error is not a default pathway; the main risk is manual reuse of ECC output by an operator.
conditions: IF agent_b is fed ECC-produced text without human review
IF ECC output is copied into downstream automation
mitigations: Require human review before reusing ECC output
Do not auto-ingest ECC artifacts into other agents
Keep generated findings separate from execution inputs
requires-engineering: add verification gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance mismatch is evidenced in the profiles: ECC lists general developer-tool data classes and allowlisted egress, while godot_rl_agents lists no data classes, no residency claims, and no regulated-data handling. Because no shared regulated data class or jurisdictional constraint is documented, a compliance breach pathway is not established.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into either agent's workflow
IF a deployment policy imposes residency or retention rules not shown in the profiles
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents
Document retention and residency rules before deployment
Review logs for accidental sensitive content
